etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Possibly from 初中後 (shochūgo).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Internationalism, ultimately from Arabic عَرَب (ʕarab); see English Arab.
First cited in Japanese to a dictionary of loanwords from 1914.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Russian интеллиге́нция (intelligéncija).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English show.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English timing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English demonstration.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Doublet of 犯す (okasu, “to commit (crime)”) and 冒す (okasu, “to risk”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 收集 (MC syuw dzip, “to collect, to gather”), from 收 (MC syuw, “to receive, to collect”) + 集 (MC dzip, “to gather”). First appears in roughly 760 CE with the spelling 聚集 in kanbun texts.
The 収集 spelling appears to be more common in modern usage.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 取(と)る (toru, “to take”) + 戻(もど)す (modosu, “to return, put back”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 嘲 (aza, “something off-color or not quite right”, compounding element found in terms such as 嘲る (azakeru, “to ridicule, to jeer at”) and 欺く (azamuku, “to deceive”), cognate with 痣 (aza, “bruise”)) + 笑う (warau, “laugh”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 圧(あつ) (atsu, “pressure”) + 力(りょく) (-ryoku, “power”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 売り (uri) + 出し (dashi, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 出す (dasu))

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese [script needed] (tukusu). Found in the Man'yōshū, completed some time after 759 CE, spelled phonetically in man'yōgana as 都久須.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 屋(や) (ya, “house”) + 敷(しき) (shiki, “building site”, short for 敷(しき)地(ち) (shikichi)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: By surface analysis, 座談(ざだん) (zadan) + 会(かい) (-kai).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 承 (shō, “agree to”) + 諾 (daku, “consent”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 招(まね)く (maneku, “to invite, call over”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Formerly ゆらく (yuraku), with the final -ku softening to -gu. Derived from adverb ゆら (yura, evoking the sound of a ball or bell rocking), itself derived from or cognate with the imperfective form of Old Japanese verb ゆる (yuru) (揺る / 淘る / 汰る, "to rock, to shake").
Compare 揺れる (yureru, “to shake; to be unsettled; to hesitate”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 植民 (shokumin, “colonization”) + 地 (chi, “land”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 殺(さつ) (satsu, “killing”) + 人(じん) (jin, “human”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 河 (ka, “river, large river”) + 川 (sen, “river”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 渡(わた)り (watari, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 渡(わた)る (wataru, “to migrate”)) + 鳥(とり) (tori, “bird”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally pronounced unvoiced, as 濯(すす)く (susuku).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 濯(ゆす)ぐ (yusugu) above.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from verb 禁(きん)ずる (kinzuru), by natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 結(むす)ぶ (musubu).
First appears in the Man'yōshū of 759 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 蜂(はち) (hachi, “bee”) + 蜜(みつ) (mitsu, “honey”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From 心 (kokoro, “heart, mind”) + 見る (miru, “to look, watch, take care”).
The み (mi) is written as an okurigana to indicate the reading of 試.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 財 (MC dzoj).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the causative form of Proto-Japonic *nonk- (“to flee, escape”). Compare 逃がす (nigasu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 面(めん) (men, “face”) + する (-suru)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 風車 (MC pjuwng tsyhae, “wind + wheel”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 風 (kaza, “wind”, the older combining form) + 車 (kuruma, “wheel”). The kuruma changes to guruma as an instance of rendaku (連濁).
